params.name: V
params.note: Offset depth. Held fixed at 1 D by the published study; FREE in this archetype.

params.name: L1
params.note: Deep-section length. Held fixed at 10 D by the study; FREE in this archetype and independent of the thick pipe length.

params.name: L2
params.note: Ramp length. Held fixed at 2.5 D by the study; FREE here. With V it sets the ramp slope, which decides how far past the deep section the shroud goes on owning contact.

params.name: L_comp
params.note: Thick pipe length. Series 1 varies it (5 D, 10 D); Series 2 fixes it at 2.5 D and moves it instead.

params.name: t_comp
params.note: The thick pipe WALL is not stated in TABLE XXXVI, XXXVIII or XL. 53 mm (2.5x parent) is carried over from the Sec.VIII wall study as the most likely value. It drives the stiffness step that IS the Type A half of this mechanism, so a wrong value changes the result -- VERIFY before using any of these anchors as ground truth.

params.name: centre_x
params.note: Thick pipe position relative to the shroud centre. 0 = midspan (X3) = the "centralised" case; Series 2 moves it to +/-3.333 D. The SHROUD also has a centre_x, fixed at 0 -- which is why every axis here names its body.

constraints.why: Two components claim contact wherever the thick pipe sits inside the shroud. Under STRICT the assembly refuses to build. LOWEST is correct here because the shroud is genuinely deeper everywhere, so there is no guess being made.

constraints.rule: V > ~0.579 D for this thick pipe
constraints.why: THE ONE PLACE where varying a dimension changes the TOPOLOGY. Above it the shroud owns contact and the thick pipe never touches a roller. Below it the thick pipe protrudes through and takes contact itself -- a different mechanical arrangement, not a smooth continuation. The threshold is the thick pipe half-OD, so it MOVES with t_comp. Published depths (0.75 D, 1.0 D) sit clear of it; the spec floor on V is 0.5 D, so the flip band is narrow but reachable.

constraints.rule: break-through at L_comp ~ 14.2 D (at L1=10 D, L2=2.5 D, V=1 D, t_comp=53 mm)
constraints.why: THE SECOND topology boundary. A thick pipe longer than the deep section does NOT immediately take contact -- the shroud RAMP is still deeper for a while, and only where the ramp rises above the thick pipe half-OD does the thick pipe break through. Closed form: the crossover sits at x = L1/2 + L2*(V - OD_comp/2)/(V - OD_pipe/2), which is 2.888 m here, so L_comp above 14.21 D flips it. Verified against a built assembly, which flips between 14.2 D and 14.5 D. It MOVES with L1, L2, V and t_comp, so it cannot be stored as a constant.

constraints.rule: thick pipe within the deep section
constraints.why: Outside it the thick pipe leaves the elevated zone and the combined mechanism stops being combined -- even while the shroud still owns contact.
The shroud L1/L2 and the thick pipe L_comp are separate lengths on separate bodies. Use parts={"SH": {...}, "TP": {...}} to move both in one call.

variables.name: L_comp
variables.note: THICK PIPE length (part TP). Series 1 axis. INDEPENDENT of the shroud lengths -- the two bodies are separately sized.

variables.name: centre_x
variables.note: THICK PIPE position (part TP). Series 2 axis: X2 catenary third, X3 midspan, X4 vessel third. NEGATIVE x is taken as the catenary side, matching X1..X5 left to right in Fig 45 -- confirm the sign against the model.

variables.name: t_comp
variables.note: THICK PIPE wall (part TP). Not stated in the source. See the VERIFY flag. It also MOVES both ownership thresholds below, since they are set by its half-OD.

variables.name: L1
variables.note: SHROUD deep-section length (part SH). Held fixed at 10 D throughout the published Type C1 study, but a free axis of the archetype -- the shroud and the thick pipe are independently sized.

variables.name: L2
variables.note: SHROUD ramp length (part SH). Fixed at 2.5 D in the published study. With V it sets the ramp slope, which decides how far past the deep section the shroud goes on owning contact.

variables.name: V
variables.note: SHROUD depth (part SH). Fixed at 1 D in the published study. Below about 0.579 D the ownership FLIPS.

absent: Stinger radius and top tension (R=85 m, T=100 MT throughout) -- SLAY-tier.
Mesh (element length = max 2xOD) -- a solver decision.
The catenary itself -- Type C1 only appears under a lay.
archetypes.notes: Shroud-only baseline for every comparison is X2 = 0.70% (anchor SH-S3-3, same shroud and same lay). Every Type C1 result exceeds it. Peak strain stays at X2 regardless of where the thick pipe sits; placing the thick pipe AT X2 is worst, because the stiffness step then lands exactly where catenary curvature is highest. The published study holds the shroud fixed (V=1 D, L1=10 D, L2=2.5 D) and moves only the thick pipe -- but the archetype leaves all six lengths free, since that is a choice of THAT study, not a property of the topology.

archetypes.title: Top structure -- EA-ST, connection system varied
archetypes.purpose: A frame carried ABOVE the pipe on a set of connectors. It owns no contact and never meets a roller; it hangs mass and restraint off the pipe through the connectors, so what governs is the connector LAYOUT, not the frame size. That is the published finding this family exists to test.

archetypes.notes: Connector types (Fig 16): F fixed, all DOF restrained. D deadband, free until the gap closes then restrained. P pin and S slot, the pin taking two translations and the slot releasing one along the pipe. The five slots exist in every case; the system chooses among them.
archetypes.connectorModellingNote: EXPECTED WARNING, not a defect. ils_builder reports that this layout's connection_system populates slots while no edes:GD-Con parts exist. That is correct and deliberate: this archetype reproduces the source paper's own analysis model, where the connector is a beam element rather than a modelled part -- the SIMPLIFIED form described in edas:shared#/connectorAttachment.twoModellingLevels. A COMPLETE layout would place a GD-Con at each populated slot, landing on a neutral edes:GD-TP welded into a split header, with associations at both ends. Do NOT copy this archetype's connector treatment into a new layout; copy its geometry and parameters, and model the connections explicitly.

definition.associationsNote: EMPTY DELIBERATELY, and this is a real piece of assembly knowledge rather than an omission. The branch-to-structure tie in an ILT is VARIANT-DEPENDENT and therefore belongs on the ANCHOR, not on the archetype: an L branch ends horizontally and meets a SIDE edge (right1), a Z turns up and meets the TOP edge (top1), and under the F1p post arrangement the post's top face is the attachment for both. Declaring one fixed association here was tried on 4Sep26 and the coincidence check correctly rejected 8 of the 12 anchors -- the archetype is the TYPE, and this relation is not a property of the type. Each anchor below carries its own where the tie is determinate.
